---
title: "Compilation, Ports, and Network Views"
subtitle: "How does one authored Plan become a selected Direct or HB network?"
toc-depth: 2
---

**Status:** `CONVERGING` implementation design.

## Compile one backend-neutral physical graph

After ParameterSet binding, Julia expands every component into oriented
physical rows and one ordered node-flux basis. The compile product carries
component, parameter, node, ground, Port, coupling, and source provenance. It
forms reciprocal C/K/G evidence for Direct and an exact JosephsonCircuits
netlist realization for HB; neither backend becomes the Plan authority.

The primitive slice follows the canonical
[branch-stamping rule](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/quantum-circuits/physical-circuit-coordinates-node-flux-basis.qmd#g2--stamp-branches-before-interpreting-matrix-entries).
Non-reference node rows use ascending canonical `node_id`; ground has no row.
Components use ascending `component_id`, and rows within one component use its
factory-schema order. For a branch oriented `terminal_1 -> terminal_2`, its
incidence vector $b$ has `+1` at the first non-ground endpoint and `-1` at the
second. A grounded endpoint is simply omitted, so a ground-to-node branch keeps
the sign implied by that same orientation.

The three primitive stamps are

$$
\Delta C=C_b\,\mathbf b\mathbf b^T,
\qquad
\Delta K=L_b^{-1}\mathbf b\mathbf b^T,
\qquad
\Delta G=R_b^{-1}\mathbf b\mathbf b^T.
$$

Every physical value is finite and strictly positive before stamping. The
compiler accumulates complete symmetric Float64 matrices in that basis; it
does not infer orientation from matrix position.

Logical Ports are absent from these intrinsic primitive C/K/G stamps. Direct
selected-network construction subsequently adds the declared Port through its
selector $B$, reference admittance $Y_0$, and source/load boundary, and then
performs the documented de-embedding. This prevents the Port reference
impedance from becoming a DUT resistor.

`run.explain()` uses this compile product to show deterministic rows and maps
without solving. In the Lessons 1–5 slice its presentation contains only the
supported evidence: Plan/request/runtime identity and bound parameters; ordered
nodes and primitive rows; C/K/G; Port `B`, `Y0`, load and selected-network
steps; Ref lineage and retained/eliminated coordinates; Direct grid or root
preflight; and, for optimization, variables, unit maps, objectives, expanded
scales, budget, seed, and algorithm IDs. It omits unsupported Composite,
PTC/transform, N-port, and HB sections instead of printing fabricated `N/A`
rows.

A compiled schematic projects the same expanded physical graph, while an
authoring schematic remains a Python projection of the Plan.

## Lower one logical Port two ways

Direct maps each Port to selector column `B`, reference admittance `Y0`, load
stamp `B Y0 B^T`, and power-wave conversion. HB lowers the same Port to exact
JosephsonCircuits `P + R` rows and solver indices. The receipt proves that node,
orientation, reference impedance, and load are equivalent across lowerings.

PTC removes only declared, evidenced `nonloading_probe` loads from the analysis
network. For driven HB it leaves the nonlinear/static balance loaded and
compensates only the linearized response, as required by the public contract.

## Replay one ordered view lineage

The selected network is formed in the public order:

1. bind parameters and compile the original Plan;
2. apply PTC to the evidenced load mask;
3. resolve automatic paired-node transforms and their induced reference matrix;
4. retain the ordered requested coordinates; and
5. eliminate the complement at zero external current using factorization or
   linear solve, never an explicit inverse.

Direct may evaluate named internal coordinates without a Port-realizable solve
view. HB and S/Y/Z solving require a Port-realizable final basis. Every failure
is attached to the step that could not prove its invariant rather than
returning a smaller or backend-specific fallback view.
